feasible.reason: The proposal is sound in its load-bearing part (no-cavity glued/potted display stack + case-open detection) and is correctly flagged as a hardware change at L/P2, so it is not refuted. But the PC13/TAMP_IN1 leg as written does NOT deliver what the entry implies: (1) a two-wire continuity loop through the flex is trivially carried through by any attacker who replaces the panel or inserts an interposer, so it detects crude removal only and does not close the accepted fake-screen/adaptive-implant residual -- the mechanical no-void stack does that work; (2) the unpowered-open detection chain is broken at three points in the current repo, beyond the 'no battery' caveat the entry already states: tamp.rs clocks RTC/TAMP from LSI only, which is not in the backup domain, so the proposed filtered TAMP_FLTCR sampling never runs while unplugged even with a supercap; init_tamp_registers clears TAMP_SR (SCR=0x0007_FFFF) before reading it, discarding a latched TAMP1F from an unpowered open; and the BHK backup-register erase has no durable effect because bhk.rs regenerates the BHK from DHUK-wrapped flash page 126 on every boot -- the real wipe is the tamp-wipe -> tzic intrusion wipe, which needs VDD and a running CPU; (3) TAMP configuration is not secured (GTZC2 intentionally unconfigured, TAMPSEC/TAMPPRIV unset, issue #50 open), so a compromised NS could clear TAMP1E/CR1 and silently disable the external tamper. None of these is a bypass of the mechanical measure, but the entry should be re-scoped as 'cost-raiser + crude-removal detector' with the firmware prerequisites listed.
feasible.corrections: 1. Re-scope the claim: the PC13 loop detects removal of the display/case only; an adaptive attacker who re-wires the loop through a fake panel or interposer is undetected. The no-cavity potted stack is the actual implant defence; state that the fake-screen residual is reduced in cost, not resolved. 2. PC13 is marked NC (pin 2) in the vendor pin table `docs/hardware/STM32U585CIU6TR Pin Functions.pdf` and the VBAT supercap is 'board not started' (`hardware_requirements.md:245`) -- both are EVT respin items; kind should be 'mixed' because firmware deltas are also required (below). 3. Unpowered detection needs an RTCCLK that survives VDD loss: switch `tamp.rs` from LSI-only (`secure/src/hw/tamp.rs:45-48, 225-258`) to the LSE 32 kHz crystal the pq1 pin table shows on pins 5/6, or use unfiltered edge mode (TAMPFLT=00 + TAMPPUDIS=1 with the external RC/pull) which detects asynchronously without RTCCLK -- but that forfeits the digital filter and raises the false-wipe risk the entry flags. 4. Firmware bug to fix first: `init_tamp_registers` writes `TAMP_SCR = 0x0007_FFFF` (`tamp.rs:270-273`) before reading SR, so a latched external-tamper flag from an open-while-unpowered event is thrown away at boot; must read-then-escalate before clearing. 5. Correct the mechanism statement: BKPR erase only kills the runtime BHK copy (`secure/src/hw/bhk.rs:5-8, 27-30` -- regenerated from flash page 126 every boot); durable effect requires `tamp-wipe` -> `tzic::trigger_intrusion_wipe` (`secure/src/nsc/mod.rs:753-762`), i.e. 'wipe on the next powered boot where the flag or the loop reads open'. 6. Prerequisite: secure the TAMP config (TAMPSEC + TAMPPRIV + TAMP_SECCFGR zone, GTZC2) -- issue #50; `sau.rs:672-673` says GTZC2 is intentionally not locked, so NS could clear `TAMP1E` today. 7. Vendor precedent is wrong in the entry's favour: Trezor's `core/embed/sec/tamper/stm32u5/tamper.c:196-200` DOES enable an external tamper (TAMP_IN2, `TAMP2E`, CR2 `TAMP2TRG`, enabled from `kernel/main.c:142`), so 'parity' is right but 'TAMP all-internal' is not. 8. Minor: the Grand Idea Studio implant was a button-injector inside the Nano S enclosure, not a board behind the screen; `hardware_requirements.md:103` saying tamp::init is 'not wired into main()' is stale (`secure/src/main.rs:1400, 4327`). 9. Serialised tamper-evident seals are routinely defeated (Argonne VAT literature); count them as cost/deterrence, not prevention. 10. Add the supercap cold-charge window (~1 min to 2 V per `brownout-hardening.md:266-269`) and ES0499 §2.2.7/2.2.8 (MONEN already set, `tamp.rs:263`) to the false-trigger receipt list.

vendor-claim.reason: Core precedent and novelty=parity hold: Foundation Passport Prime ships screen/disassembly tamper detection with key erasure (vendor statements), Coldcard ships a see-through case + SE-driven GENUINE/CAUTION LEDs, no evidence of Ledger enclosure tamper detection was found, and pq1's TAMP driver really is internal-only (no TAMP1E/TAMP2E) with the case-switch row 'board not started'. PC13 is confirmed as TAMP_IN1 (and TAMP_OUT2) on STM32U585CI and is NC on the pq1 board. However the Trezor characterization is wrong in direction: the cited tamper.c is NOT all-internal — it has full external TAMP_IN2 (PA0) support compiled for T3W1 (Safe 7) with a prodtest 'tamper-read' command; what is true is that the shipped production path explicitly DISABLES it (secmon calls tamper_external_disable(), commit 5782cb9e54 2025-11-26, after enable-in-production 2025-06-18 and removal 2025-11-18; the kernel's PRODUCTION enable is dead on T3W1 because SECURE_MODE is not a T3W1 model feature). Also the threat field's 'Ledger implant was a concealed board behind the screen' is not supported by the sources I could read (the 2021 Nano X implant was a flash drive wired to the USB pads; the 2026 Joe Grand implant's placement could not be verified — slides exceed fetch limit) and the cited Coldcard blog does not mention the clear case (coldcard.com/docs/physical-notes does). These are corrections, not a refutation of the proposal or its novelty rating.
vendor-claim.corrections: 1) vendor_precedent Trezor: replace 'TAMP all-internal-confirmed mode' with: 'Trezor driver supports one external tamper input (TAMP_IN2 = PA0, level-high trigger, TAMPER_INPUT_2 defined for all three T3W1/Safe 7 board revisions, prodtest `tamper-read` reads it); internal tampers ITAMP1/2/3/5/6/7/8/9/11/12/13 in confirmed mode (CR3=0); IRQ response = clear TAMP2E + RSOD panic/reboot (HW erases backup domain/RAM), not a firmware-driven wipe. In the shipped production path the external input is explicitly DISABLED: secmon/main.c:113-114 `tamper_init(); tamper_external_disable();` (commit 5782cb9e54, 2025-11-26) — the kernel/main.c:139-142 `#if PRODUCTION tamper_external_enable()` sits under `#ifdef SECURE_MODE`, and T3W1 model.toml (secmon=true) does not list `secure_mode`, so it is dead on Safe 7. History: ea889e109e (2025-06-18) enabled external tamper in secmon+kernel under PRODUCTION and removed it from the bootloader; 7fd49c9cd7 (2025-11-18) removed it from secmon; 5782cb9e54 made the disable explicit. Net: Trezor hardware has the line, firmware does not arm it in production — still parity-or-behind for D-08, so novelty='parity' stands.' Also the Trezor path has moved to core/embed/sys/tamper/ in newer commits (the checked-out snapshot 6ab39e95 still has core/embed/sec/tamper/stm32u5/tamper.c). 2) Passport Prime source: docs.foundation.xyz/glossary only says 'active tamper detection that monitors whether the device has been physically opened or modified ... erases all sensitive data including your Master Key ... cannot be overridden'; the screen-removal specific claim comes from Foundation's 'Passport Prime Audit Response 2025' ('the device's display ... is protected by tamper detection pins that would trigger security responses upon disassembly attempts') — the PDF URL foundation.xyz/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/Passport-Prime-Audit-Response-2025.pdf returned 404 for me; quote obtained via search snippet only; foundation.xyz/blog/passport-prime-security-audit confirms debug pads are 'hidden and protected by tamper detection'. Say 'erases Master Key' rather than 'factory reset'. 3) Coldcard source: the cited blog.coinkite.com/understanding-mk4-security-model/ supports the SE-driven LED ('The light is controlled by the secure element and enforced cryptographically') and the tamper-evident bag but does NOT mention a clear case; cite coldcard.com/docs/physical-notes/ ('COLDCARDs have see-through cases making physical attempts to alter the hardware glaringly obvious'). Coldcard has no case-open switch. 4) Ledger threat text: the known 2021 Nano X implant was an off-the-shelf flash drive wired to the USB pads (phishing lure), not a board behind the screen; Joe Grand's 2026 'Reverse Engineering a Ledger Nano X Hardware Implant' (Cortex-M0+ implant) placement unverified — slides >10 MB, portfolio/hardwear.io pages give no placement. Reword to 'implants have been found inside genuine Nano X units' unless the slides are read. 'Ledger: none (procedural only)' is an absence-from-search claim; note Ledger's Stax/Flex mitigation for fake panels is the SE-driven Secure Screen, not enclosure tamper. 5) Pin facts: embassy stm32-data STM32U585CI: TAMP IN1=PC13, OUT2=PC13, IN2=PA0, OUT1=PA0. pq1 pin table: PC13 = NC (pin 2), PA0 = LEFT KEY, PA6/PA10 = NC. So only PASSIVE tamper on PC13 is possible with the current pin map (active tamper needs a TAMP_OUTx partner; PA0 is taken, PA6/PA10 are not TAMP pins) — state that; ST notes open/short detection is an active-tamper feature. 6) repo_evidence line refs: tamp.rs ITAMP enable constants are at 194-204, CR1 set_bits at 288-300, IER at 313-325 — no TAMP1E/TAMP2E/CR2 anywhere (confirmed); FLTCR already set at 272-278. VBAT is bonded (pin 1) but the supercap is 'board not started' (hardware_requirements.md:245), consistent with the stated 'open while unpowered only wipes at next power-up' risk — the BHK master in flash page 126 reloads on cold boot, so only a persistent flag/loop-read on boot gives the wipe.
